problem: Embodied-AI simulators before 2019 tied the task, the platform and the 3D dataset together, which made cross-dataset and cross-task experiments impractical. They hard-coded agent and sensor configurations and rendered at only 10-300 fps, so large-scale RL was infeasible. As a result, prior learning-vs-SLAM comparisons for PointGoal navigation (Mishkin et al., Kojima & Deng) used only about 5-10M steps and concluded that classic SLAM dominates.
motivation: Training robots in the real world is slow, unsafe, expensive and hard to reproduce, and simulators are expected to play the role datasets played for 'internet AI'. A fragmented simulator landscape hinders reproducibility and community benchmarks. The authors also observe that low simulator throughput makes conclusions from short training runs unreliable ('has the learning converged to trust the comparisons?').
key_idea: Build a unified, dataset-agnostic, very fast simulator (Habitat-Sim, >10k fps on one GPU) plus a modular task/agent API (Habitat-API), and use the resulting throughput to train PointGoal agents on 75M steps; at that scale, learned depth agents beat classic SLAM.
insight: Conclusions about learned vs. classic navigation depend on training scale. At 5M frames SLAM looks dominant, but RL (PPO) Depth matches SLAM at about 10M frames on Gibson and 30M on MP3D, then surpasses it (Fig. 3). Depth alone beats RGBD by 0.09-0.16 SPL, SLAM by 0.15-0.28 and RGB by 0.13-0.33, because PointNav needs only free-space reasoning and high-entropy RGB overfits; RGB barely beats Blind when GPS+Compass is available. Only depth agents generalize across datasets, and Gibson-trained agents beat MP3D-trained ones even on MP3D (Depth 0.68 vs 0.54 SPL), since easier, shorter episodes give reward earlier; this suggests curriculum learning. Low-level task choices also matter: rejection-sampling near-straight episodes (ratio in [1,1.1] reduced from 37% to 10%) is needed or metrics are inflated, and static goal + idealized GPS+Compass is separated from simulator design.
method: Habitat-Sim: C++ simulator on the Magnum middleware. A hierarchical SceneGraph gives generic dataset ingestion (Matterport3D, Gibson, Replica), a multi-attachment 'uber-shader' renders RGB/depth/semantic outputs in one pass, and agents/sensors are configurable. It reaches thousands of fps single-thread and >10k fps multi-process; OpenGL-CUDA interop allows direct GPU→GPU frame sharing.

Habitat-API: modular Python library built on Task / Episode / Environment / Dataset abstractions. It supports PointNav, EQA and VLN-style tasks, RL/IL/SLAM baselines and standard metrics (SPL), and can use other simulator backends.

PointGoal task specification: cylinder agent (0.2 m diameter, 1.5 m tall); actions are forward 0.25 m, turn 10° and stop. Motion is continuous with sliding collisions and noise-free actuation. The goal is static and the agent has idealized GPS+Compass. Episodes allow up to 500 actions; success is stop within 0.2 m geodesic; metric is SPL.

Episode dataset generation: Matterport3D splits plus 106 curated Gibson scenes (quality rating ≥4). GDSP is kept in 1-30 m. Episodes with geodesic/Euclidean ratio in [1,1.1] are rejection-sampled, which lowers near-straight episodes from 37% to 10% on Gibson.

RL (PPO) baseline: 3-layer CNN (8×8, 4×4, 3×3 conv + linear) embeds RGB/Depth/RGBD, concatenated with the goal vector and fed to a GRU actor and a linear critic. Reward is s + (d_{t-1}-d_t) + λ with s=10, λ=-0.01. Training runs to 75M steps with 8 (Gibson) / 6 (MP3D) workers, about 2267 GPU-hours total, 5 seeds.
Classic and hand-coded baselines: ORB-SLAM2-based SLAM agent from Mishkin et al., plus Random, Forward-only and Goal-follower.

Habitat Challenge (CVPR 2019): participants submit Docker containers via EvalAI and are evaluated remotely on unseen environments. Planned future changes are static goals only, a PyRobot-derived actuation noise model, and RGB/depth sensor noise.

setting.training_data: Habitat PointGoal episodes generated by the authors: Gibson 72 train scenes (4.9M episodes) or Matterport3D 58 train scenes (4.8M episodes); 75M agent steps of on-policy RL experience per model (additional 800M-step runs in supplement)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB and/or depth, 256×256, 90° FOV, camera at 1.5 m + idealized GPS+Compass (relative goal vector)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN_LEFT / TURN_RIGHT 10° / STOP (continuous state with sliding collisions, noise-free actuation)
setting.simulator: Habitat (Habitat-Sim) with Gibson and Matterport3D scenes
setting.privileged: idealized noise-free GPS+Compass (perfect localization) and noise-free actuation; no GT map

numbers_note: SPL and success are printed as fractions (e.g. 0.79), converted here to 0-100. The Blind RL (PPO) agent on MP3D test (SPL 0.25, Succ 0.35) and the MP3D→Gibson cross-dataset results (Figure 5: Blind 0.28, RGB 0.25, Depth 0.56, RGBD 0.44 SPL) were omitted because of the variant limit. Training curves on val are shown only in Figure 3. The 800M-step results appear only as relative differences in the supplement text (RGB > Blind by 0.06/0.03 SPL; RGBD > SLAM on MP3D by 0.16 SPL). The noisy-depth study reports only SPL drops (0.13 for depth-RL, 0.02 for SLAM on Gibson-val). No NE/OSR/TL reported. Episodes are the authors' own Habitat PointGoal datasets (later known as PointNav v1).
results: On the Habitat PointGoal test sets, the RL (PPO) Depth agent trained for 75M steps scores the best result: 0.79 SPL / 0.89 success on Gibson and 0.54 / 0.69 on MP3D. It beats the ORB-SLAM2-based classic agent of Mishkin et al. (0.51/0.62 Gibson, 0.39/0.47 MP3D), RL RGBD (0.70, 0.42) and RL RGB (0.46, 0.30). This reverses prior conclusions, which were based on about 5M steps. Only depth-equipped agents generalize across datasets, and Gibson-trained agents outperform MP3D-trained ones even on MP3D. Habitat-Sim renders about 4,000 fps single-process and >10,000 fps multi-process at 128×128 RGB, 2-3 orders of magnitude faster than prior realistic indoor simulators.
limitations: Experiments use noise-free actuation and idealized GPS+Compass (perfect localization), which inflates PointNav performance relative to realistic settings; a learned depth agent trained without noise loses 0.13 SPL under noisy depth.

Only PointGoal navigation is benchmarked, with a single small CNN+GRU PPO architecture and a single SLAM pipeline, so the learning-vs-SLAM conclusion covers representative instances rather than the whole families.
The first release lacks physics and object interaction, and the Gibson subset is manually curated (106 of 572 scenes).
